subject.title: feat(imessage): native poll controls for approval prompts

question: Should capable iMessage bridge installations automatically prefer native approval polls, while retaining tapback and manual-command fallbacks for unsupported or unconfirmed deliveries?
rationale: This is a user-visible default change on a privileged approval interaction. The implementation can preserve compatibility, but repository policy requires maintainer intent for the permanent product behavior.

options.title: Adopt capability-gated polls
options.body: Approve native polls as the eligible-installation default after confirming the released bridge contract, fallbacks, and current-head CI.

options.title: Keep reactions as the default
options.body: Require an explicit opt-in or defer native polls if the existing tapback interaction should remain the default approval UX.

recommendation.title: Adopt capability-gated polls
recommendation.body: Approve native polls as the eligible-installation default after confirming the released bridge contract, fallbacks, and current-head CI.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work connects the channel’s delegated/direct authority model to the narrow Gateway approval runtime used by this change.
